keyTakeaways: Tell people in order before posting: children from a previous relationship, then parents and siblings, then grandparents and best friends, per Emily Post's guidance.
Keep single-photo captions under 15 words: 48.3% of SubhSandesh shared pages are opened on a phone.
Write about your partner, not yourself: a five-study 2019 PLOS ONE paper found partner-focused online posts avoided the intimacy drop linked to deep personal disclosure.
Before posting a ring close-up, crop house numbers, street signs, labels and plates, and drop any home location tag.
Halloween is Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027; posting the next morning, after the calls, is usually kinder.

faqs.question: Is it okay to announce an engagement on Halloween night?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the people closest to you have heard first. Halloween is Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027, and many relatives are busy at parties or at the door that evening, so posting the next morning after your calls is often the kinder choice.

faqs.question: Can I post my ring photo before telling my parents?
faqs.answer: Etiquette says no. Emily Post's guidance puts children from a previous relationship first, then parents and siblings, then grandparents and best friends, and only after that the wider circle, so a parent should never learn it from a feed.

faqs.question: Should the engagement caption be about me or about my partner?
faqs.answer: Lean towards your partner and the relationship. A 2019 PLOS ONE paper by Lee, Gillath and Miller found that deep personal disclosure to a wide online audience went with lower intimacy and satisfaction, while posts focused on the partner and the relationship did not show that effect.

faqs.question: How long should a Halloween engagement caption be?
faqs.answer: For a single photo, aim for under 15 words so the line survives a phone screen, where 48.3% of SubhSandesh shared pages are opened. Save the long version for a carousel, where people expect the full story.

faqs.question: Is a costume photo too silly for an engagement announcement?
faqs.answer: Not if the caption makes clear the ring is real. Name the costumes in the caption and keep the joke about the two of you, so nobody mistakes the ring for a prop.

faqs.question: What should I check in a ring photo before posting it?
faqs.answer: Look at the background, not just the ring: house numbers, street signs, delivery labels, car plates and a location tag on your home address. The UK National Cyber Security Centre advises thinking about who can see a post and which details followers do not need but criminals could use.

faqs.question: How do we tell grandparents who are not on social media?
faqs.answer: Call them or tell them in person before anything goes online, using a short opener such as "Family first, internet second: we're getting married." A printed photo in a card is a good follow-up for a grandparent who does not use a smartphone.

faqs.question: When should we hold an engagement party after a Halloween proposal?
faqs.answer: Anna Post's guidance on emilypost.com says engagement parties are typically held within one to three months of the engagement, with invitations sent two to four weeks ahead. For a 31 October proposal that points to a party between November and the end of January.

faqs.question: Can I use the Halloween greeting page to share our engagement news?
faqs.answer: Yes, for one person at a time. The /happy-halloween page takes up to six photos and a letter, and its closing question is editable up to 60 characters, so you could ask a best friend to stand beside you at the wedding; it is not a group announcement tool.

faqs.question: Do we need to wait to announce if one of us was married before?
faqs.answer: Yes. Emily Post's advice is never to announce an engagement until a former marriage has been dissolved by divorce or annulment.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Engagement Captions and How to Announce the News

The right Halloween engagement caption names the photo you are posting and goes up only after your closest people have heard the news by phone or in person. Keep it short: on SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages get opened on a phone, where lines under 15 words survive the crop, and keep it guarded, as 38.5% of our creators add a password before sharing anything personal. Below: 56 original captions in seven photo groups, a story template, who to tell first and a ring-photo privacy check.

## What makes a Halloween engagement caption work?

A Halloween engagement caption is the text posted with the first public photo of an engagement made close to 31 October. It announces a commitment, so it borrows the season without turning the ring into a costume joke.

Research favours captions about your partner. [Papp, Danielewicz and Cayemberg (2012)](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/21988733) studied 58 dating couples: men listing a partnered status, and women showing their partner in their profile picture, went with higher satisfaction. [Toma and Choi (2015)](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/26167834) linked posting photos together to rising commitment and to still being a couple six months on; for both, only abstracts were read.

The focus of the post matters. Across five studies, [Lee, Gillath and Miller (2019, *PLOS ONE*)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC6398828) found deep personal disclosure to a wide online audience went with lower intimacy and satisfaction, but centring the post on the partner and the relationship removed that effect.

## 56 Halloween engagement captions, by photo type

All lines here were written for this page. Swap in names where you see brackets.

### 1. Ring close-up captions (8)

For a hand shot with black nails or a carved pumpkin. Keep it shorter than the photo.

- Black polish, new sparkle, same hand that carved the pumpkin.
- One ring, one pumpkin, one very shaky hand.
- My manicure was planned for Halloween. The ring was not.
- The only thing glowing brighter than the jack-o'-lantern tonight.
- Swapped my plastic spider ring for a permanent one.
- Candlelight, a carved pumpkin and a question I keep answering yes to.
- New jewellery, same old sweetheart.
- Exhibit A: proof this ghost story ended well.

### 2. Proposal moment captions (8)

For the photo snapped mid-question. Add one unseen detail.

- [Name] knelt in a pumpkin patch and I forgot every word except yes.
- The fog machine was a nice touch. The question was better.
- Somewhere between the haunted maze and the cider stand, everything changed.
- Ten seconds before this photo I thought we were just picking pumpkins.
- Asked on the spookiest night of the year. Never felt less scared.
- 31 October, 8:40 pm: the night stopped being about costumes.
- The scariest part was the pause before my answer. It lasted one second.
- Our friends knew. The bats knew. I was the last to find out.

### 3. Costume engagement captions (8)

At a party, the costumes are the story. Name them so the ring isn't mistaken for a prop.

- We dressed as a vampire and a vampire hunter. The hunter got caught.
- The witch said yes. The cauldron is thrilled.
- A skeleton proposed tonight, and I'm keeping him, bones and all.
- Two ghosts walked into a party and walked out engaged.
- Yes, we're still in costume. No, the ring is not part of it.
- An hour on that mummy wrap, thirty seconds on the question that mattered.
- Proof the scarecrow had a brain after all: he asked me.
- Our couple costume for next year: fiancés.

### 4. October save-the-date teaser captions (8)

Post a teaser once you have a month. Guests book October early: [Emily Post lists it among the six most popular wedding months](https://emilypost.com/advice/congratulationsyoure-engaged).

- Mark next October. Costumes optional, cake mandatory.
- Same month, one year on: we're getting married in October.
- Save the night. Black tie or black cape, both accepted.
- The pumpkins will be on the porch again when we say our vows.
- Keep your autumn free. The wedding will be haunted in the nicest way.
- Date coming soon. Season already confirmed: the spooky one.
- Hold the last weekend of next October for us.
- One year after the question, same season, a few more guests.

### 5. Funny Halloween engagement captions (8)

Joke about the two of you, never the ring's price. All clean enough for a grandparent.

- Engaged on Halloween, so every anniversary comes with discount candy.
- [Name] hid the ring in my candy bucket. I nearly ate the box.
- Off the market, still on the candy hunt.
- Engaged to the person who steals my peanut butter cups. Love forgives.
- We will never forget our anniversary. Every shop decorates for it.
- Proposed to by a dinosaur. Marrying a T. rex with excellent taste.
- Ring fits. Costume doesn't. Priorities.
- The answer was a very loud, very undignified YES.

### 6. Elegant and gothic engagement captions (9)

For moody photos in black lace, go quieter. Let the light do the talking.

- By candlelight and a crescent moon, I promised [Name] all my Octobers.
- Dark velvet, cold air, warm hands.
- Every autumn from now on belongs to us.
- Asked beneath bare branches, while the whole night held its breath.
- Some love stories start in spring. Ours chose the season of shadows.
- A raven-black evening and the brightest question of my life.
- Forever, sealed in candle wax and October frost.
- Lace, lanterns and a yes whispered in the dark.
- Bound by moonlight and one small promise.

### 7. Family announcement wording for grandparents (7)

For a text, card or call, not a public post. Use them as openers.

- Nani, Grandpa: before anyone online, we wanted you to know. We're engaged.
- You showed us what a long marriage looks like. Now we're starting ours.
- The ring came on Halloween, but your blessing is what we were waiting for.
- We got engaged on 31 October and called you before the photo went anywhere.
- Grandma, you always said October was lucky. You were right.
- Family first, internet second: we're getting married.
- Remember the kid you took trick-or-treating as a bedsheet ghost? She's engaged.

### 8. "We got engaged on Halloween" story template

A carousel post is where people expect the full story. Cut any line that doesn't fit.

> We got engaged on Halloween, and here is how it happened.
> [Name] said we were going to [place] for [the plan I believed].
> At [time], [the moment I realised].
> I said yes before [funny detail].
> Thank you to [helpers], and to [our parents], who heard first.
> Wedding: [season and year]. Costumes: under discussion.

## Halloween engagement announcement: who to tell before you post

Etiquette sets an order, and it runs before the caption. In a 2008 column republished by Emily Post, [Anna Post gives the sequence](https://emilypost.com/advice/inside-weddings-celebrating-your-engagement): children from a previous relationship first, then parents and siblings (asked to keep it quiet for a few days), then grandparents and best friends, then the wider family.

After a public proposal, call anyone close who missed it. Halloween is Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027, when relatives are busy at the door, so post the next morning, after the calls.

## Ring-photo privacy: 4 things to check before posting

A ring close-up is often shot at home, where the background says more than the caption. The UK National Cyber Security Centre's [social media guidance, first published 24 January 2019](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/guidance/social-media-how-to-use-it-safely), asks you to weigh who can see a post and which details followers don't need but criminals could use.

- **House number or street sign** beside your porch pumpkins: crop it out.
- **Location tag** on a home address: tag the city instead.
- **Envelopes, delivery labels and car plates** in the frame.
- **Audience setting**: public or close friends, chosen before posting.

## Halloween engagement caption types compared

| Photo or announcement | Tone | Who to tell first | Example line |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ring close-up | Playful, short | Parents and siblings, by call | "One ring, one pumpkin, one very shaky hand." |
| Proposal moment | Warm, one detail | Anyone who helped plan, then parents | "The fog machine was a nice touch. The question was better." |
| Costume photo | Funny | Best friends likely to comment | "Two ghosts walked into a party and walked out engaged." |
| October save-the-date | Informative | Both families, before the date is public | "Save the night. Black tie or black cape, both accepted." |
| Grandparents message | Gentle, private | Grandparents directly, never via the feed | "Family first, internet second: we're getting married." |

The more private the audience, the more personal the wording. Nobody on that list should meet the news in a caption.

## A private version for the people who hear it first

Some people on that list deserve more than a text: the [Halloween greeting page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is a one-person page with up to six photos and a letter the recipient reads by flashlight after knocking three times. Its closing question defaults to "Will you be my boo?" but is editable up to 60 characters, so in best-friend mode it can ask "Will you stand next to me next October?", and you get an email the first time they answer.

For parents or grandparents in another city, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) adds a voice note of up to 60 seconds and an optional unlock time: until then, the link shows only their name and a countdown. Pages built on SubhSandesh average 11.1 views each, so expect repeat visits.

## When a public engagement caption is the wrong choice

Emily Post's advice is blunt: never announce an engagement until a former marriage has been dissolved by divorce or annulment. If that paperwork is open, the caption waits.

A SubhSandesh page is also the wrong tool for a grandparent without a smartphone, where a call or a printed photo in a card wins, and its interface is English only. These are one-person greeting pages, not invitations for a crowd, so use printed cards or a wedding website once real save-the-dates go out.

## Sources

- Papp et al. (2012), *Cyberpsychology, Behavior, and Social Networking*, abstract.
- Toma and Choi (2015), same journal, abstract.
- Lee, Gillath and Miller (4 March 2019), *PLOS ONE*.
- Anna Post (2008), Emily Post Institute.
- Emily Post Institute, "Congratulations—You're Engaged!" (undated).
- NCSC (24 January 2019), social media guidance.

auditReport.honestAssessment: The SERP is thin: two Elite Daily lists from 2019 and 2020 and a page of hijacked-subdomain spam, none of which covers who to tell first, family wording, ring-photo privacy or any research, so this page offers what an answer engine cannot get from them. It cannot overcome Elite Daily's domain authority, the lines are only as good as their originality, and the first-party numbers are platform-wide, not engagement-specific; expect months, not weeks.
